title: What a step-up SIP is
objectives: Explain the three reasons a flat SIP is not enough.
body_md:
A step-up (or top-up) SIP increases the instalment automatically at a set interval, by a fixed amount or a percentage. The investor decides the rule once, and the AMC applies it.

## Why a flat SIP is not enough

- Inflation erodes it. At 6% inflation, ₹10,000 a month in 20 years buys only what about ₹3,100 buys today.
- Income usually grows. A SIP that stays flat becomes a smaller share of income every year.
- Compounding rewards it. Later, bigger instalments still have years to grow.

## The one line to remember

Save more tomorrow, automatically. Tie each step-up to a raise, so the client never feels the money go.

## What this module covers

The two ways to set a step-up and how AMCs run them; the numbers; who it suits and how much to raise; how to set it up, cap it and review it; and the habits that stop clients from ever doing it.
example: Riya, 24, can invest ₹5,000 a month and expects 10% raises. A 10% yearly step-up, timed just after each increment, keeps the SIP in line with her income without a single decision after the first.
say: A step-up SIP raises your instalment automatically, so you don't have to remember.
We'll set it once and it happens on its own.
never: A step-up guarantees you'll reach the goal.

o: A SIP that rises automatically at set intervals
A SIP that switches funds every year
